subtype: Approach: tracking which pieces get attention [Revision]
passage: Jagdish, you asked how I improved the portfolio, and the honest answer is: I watched. I'm Sachin, and for two weeks I checked which projects people actually opened, since the site kept a simple count. Twelve visits went to the chess timer that had a live link. Two went to the report analyser. The recruiter emails I got mentioned the timer every time. So I moved it to the very first spot on the page, above everything else. And I noticed the pattern, so I spent a weekend putting one more project online with a link that works. Now two of my projects can be tried by anyone. The count of visits tripled, and one recruiter wrote, "I clicked the link and it worked."

qa.q: How many visits went to the chess timer?
qa.a: Twelve visits went to the chess timer.

qa.q: What did Sachin feel when noticing which project people opened?
qa.a: Sachin felt curious and motivated, seeing a clear pattern that pointed to what to do next.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Sachin add to learn more, and why?
qa.a: Sachin could ask two recruiters what they looked at first, because visit counts show clicks but not the reasons behind them.

qa.q: How might a recruiter see the live link?
qa.a: A recruiter can try the project at once and see it work, which builds trust faster than reading a description.

grounding: Shows watching which portfolio pieces get attention and reorganising around the deployed project.

subtype: Approach: tracking which pieces get attention [Revision]
passage:
I'm Jyoti, Payal's roommate, and I watched this happen over about a month. Payal put her portfolio online in September with four projects and a free counter that shows which pages get opened.
Every Sunday she'd sit on her bed and read the numbers out loud, half to herself. 'Recruiters opened it twenty-three times. Twenty-one of those were the bus-tracking project.' The other three projects, the ones with just code and screenshots, barely got clicks.
'It's the only one with a live link,' she said the second Sunday. 'People want to try it, not read about it.'
That week she moved the bus tracker to the top. Then she spent two evenings getting her expense-splitting app online too, with its own live link. By the end of October, both live projects were being opened. I don't know if it will get her a job, but she stopped guessing.

qa.q: How many of the twenty-three opens were for the bus-tracking project?
What does Payal's remark 'People want to try it, not read about it' suggest about how she felt?
qa.a: She seems curious and a little surprised by the numbers, and confident she has found a clear signal to act on.

qa.q: What else could Payal track to keep improving the site?
qa.a: How long visitors stay on each live project, so she can see which one holds attention and put her effort there.

qa.q: How do these Sundays look to Jyoti?
qa.a: Jyoti watches Payal move from guessing to acting on the numbers, while staying unsure whether it will lead to a job.

grounding: Shows a student noticing that recruiters mostly open the project with a live link, moving it to the top and putting another project online.

passage:
Week 1, Monday. Gargi sends her portfolio link to eight recruiters and turns on a simple visit counter. She is proudest of the long write-up about her sorting-algorithm study.
Week 3, Friday. She checks the counter with her friend Aadhya. Fourteen visits. Twelve went straight to the weather-alert app, the only project with a live demo. The algorithm write-up: one visit, eleven seconds.
'Ouch,' Aadhya says.
'No, it's useful,' Gargi says slowly. 'They want something they can click.'
Week 5, Sunday. The weather-alert app now sits at the top of the page. Gargi has spent two weekends putting her attendance tracker online as well, with a 'try it' button. The algorithm study is still there, lower down. That night the counter shows three new visits, all to the live projects.

qa.q: How long did the one visit to the algorithm write-up last?
What was Gargi feeling when she saw the algorithm write-up got one visit?
qa.a: She was probably disappointed, since it was her proudest piece, but she turned that into curiosity and called the numbers useful.

qa.q: What would you change next if Gargi still wants the algorithm study noticed?
qa.a: Add a small live demo or an interactive chart to it, so it becomes something recruiters can click like the other two.

qa.q: How does the counter look to Aadhya on Friday?
qa.a: Aadhya first sees it as a blow, saying 'Ouch', then watches Gargi treat it as information.

grounding: Shows a student seeing that recruiters open only the live project, moving it to the top and putting a second project online.
